nimi.en: Immersive Software Engineering and AI, Bachelor of Science (Technology) (3 yrs), autumn 2027

kuvaus.en:
Turn your passion for technology into a career. The Bachelor’s Programme in Immersive Software Engineering and AI combines academic learning and projects with two internships to prepare you for the future of software development. You’ll gain expertise in software engineering, AI, and business while working in an international environment connected to cutting-edge research and industry.

No one becomes an IT professional developing new technology by chance – it takes dedication and consistent effort. That’s why this bachelor’s programme mirrors real working life and is designed much like the way doctors are trained. Instead of memorization or traditional exams, learning focuses on exploring concepts through meaningful activities.

You’ll work daily in small, collaborative groups guided by academic experts. Through immersive, project-based learning, you’ll grow into a skilled technology developer.

Software engineering combines logical reasoning with practical application. AI plays an increasing role in coding, but it’s not a shortcut to success. Those who thrive are the ones who can both create software and use AI effectively as a tool.

The Immersive Software Engineering and AI programme is a three-year degree (180 ECTS). The curriculum includes:

  • Software engineering,
  • Artificial intelligence,
  • Mathematics,
  • Entrepreneurship and business, including insights into the European and Finnish business network, and
  • Finnish language, society and culture, covering the Nordic region and the European Union.

The programme includes two four-month internships in companies developing modern IT systems. If you pass the recruitment interview with a participating company, which will take place shortly before the internship, your internship will be paid. These internships allow you to apply what you’ve learned and continue developing your skills in real professional environments.

Your studies prepare you for demanding roles in the IT industry. To support integration into local working life, the programme also includes Finnish language studies.

No scholarships are offered for the first year. A tuition fee scholarship of 6,000€ will be granted for your second and third year of studies if you complete at least 55 ECTS during the preceding academic year (and are liable to pay tuition fees).

For more information, please see: Tuition fees and scholarships (jyu.fi)

maksullisuusKuvaus.en:
A 1,500 € early bird discount from the first year tuition fee is offered to those who accept their study place within 14 days and pay the annual tuition fee by the deadline. You are not required to pay tuition fees if you are a citizen of an EU/EEA country or Switzerland or hold a specific type of residence permit in Finland. For more information, please see: Tuition fees and scholarships (jyu.fi)
The full tuition fee in the bachelor's programme is 16,000 € per year. For more information, please see: Scholarships and tuition fees (jyu.fi)

teksti.en: Please see further information on the programme-specific web page.

Completing this programme equips you with the expertise to succeed in diverse professional environments. Possible career paths include:

  • R&D Engineer – Innovating and prototyping next-generation technologies
  • Software Developer or Architect – Designing complex, scalable systems for critical applications
  • Entrepreneur – Launching your own high-tech startup or pursuing an innovation-driven career
  • Technology Consultant or Product Manager – Leading digital transformation and product innovation across industries
  • Academic Researcher – Advancing to Master’s or doctoral studies in scientific and technological fields

The programme works closely with industry partners in the Finnish IT sector. From early on, you’ll have the chance to start building your career by working on real-world projects. The first four-month internship takes place already after your first year of studies.
With a diverse community of teachers, researchers, and students worldwide, the faculty fosters international collaboration in research, education, and industry.

At the University of Jyväskylä’s Faculty of Information Technology—one of Finland’s largest IT units—you’ll study in a programme closely linked to cutting-edge research. Our expertise spans software engineering and emerging areas like quantum programming and AI, preparing you for the future of technology.

You will complete your bachelor’s thesis during the second four-month internship. This gives you the chance to work on topics that matter to the company you join. Your thesis won’t be just an academic exercise—it combines academic skills with real-world needs.

pohjakoulutusvaatimusTarkenne.en: If the degree you use to prove your eligibility is still incomplete at the time of applying, you can be conditionally admitted. In this case, you must graduate from your previous degree and submit your final educational documents in time to meet the given deadline. This deadline will be announced on our website: How to apply for international bachelor's programmes.

kuvaus.en:
The required application attachments are listed below. Some attachments may be optional or apply only to some applicant groups. Any documents not listed below will not be considered in the evaluation process.

On the application form, you will also have a chance to provide a link to your online portfolio or other material (such as a GitHub portfolio). This is optional. The link must be informed on the appropriate question of the application form by 21 January 2027 3:00 pm (UTC+2) to be considered.

If any compulsory attachments have not been submitted according to our instructions or in time to meet the given deadline(s), your application will be deemed ineligible and not processed further. The detailed instructions for attachments will be published on the

University’s website before the application period opens. The instructions may change between application rounds, and you must make sure to comply with the requirements for the correct round.

1. Educational documents proving your eligibility for bachelor’s-level studies

If the documents are issued in a language other than English, Finnish, or Swedish, an official translation into one of these languages is required in addition to the original language version.

2. Copy of a valid passport (if needed)
A copy of the identification page(s) of a valid passport with the applicant’s name, date of birth, and nationality. If you do not hold a valid passport, another official identification document (such as an identity card or driver’s license) stating the same information is accepted.

Please note: As a part of the application process, you may be invited to an interview. At the beginning of the interview, you must prove your identity by presenting your passport, official photo ID card, or driver’s license to the camera. An expired document is accepted if it expired less than a year ago from the start date of the application period. If you do not identify yourself in this manner, your application will be deemed ineligible.

If you are a Finnish citizen: You are not required to upload a separate identification document to your application form. However, you must prove your identity at the start of the interview as described above.

3. Copy of a residence permit card (if applicable)

A copy of both sides of the residence permit card. The document is required only if you, the applicant, hold one of the following: a valid residence permit in Finland of type A (that is not based on studies), P, P-EU, EU Blue Card, or a certificate of the permanent right of residence of a UK citizen in Finland, or residence card for a family member of an EU or UK citizen residing in Finland.

hakuNimi.en: Joint Application to Higher Education, Spring 2027

tietoja.en:
All applicants who have submitted an application by the given deadline, and paid the application fee (if applicable) are invited to participate in an online exam.

Before the actual exam, you can test the online admission test platform (called TIM) to ensure you are familiar with the system. The platform is open for testing between 2 - 5 February 2027. You can access the platform at: tim.pm/iseai. After the application period ends, you will receive a password by email to the address provided in your Studyinfo application. Use your email and password to log in and test the platform. Please check your junk or promotions folder if the email does not appear in your inbox.

It is strongly recommended to test the online admission test platform before the actual exam week so that you are familiar with the system before you start doing the actual exam.

The actual online exam will be open from 10 February to 11 February 2027.

ohjeetErityisjarjestelyihin.en:
It is possible to apply for individual arrangements if you have a diagnosed disability or medical condition that affects your ability to participate in the admission process, such as hearing or visual impairment or dyslexia.

If you have needs that should be considered during the admission process, you must submit a written request for individual arrangements and the necessary attachment(s) to the JYU Admission Services by 28 January 2027 at 3:00 p.m. UTC+2.

Please see the list of required documents and further instructions from our website. Pay careful attention to the document content requirements regarding the expert statement (e.g. medical certificate).
